summary.title: MolmoMotion: Forecasting Point Trajectories in 3D with Language Instruction

setting_and_object.category: Task formulation with accompanying dataset, benchmark, and model (full stack)

details: Existing motion forecasting representations are either category-specific (parametric human/hand/rigid-body models), camera-entangled (2D image-plane tracks), or expensive and hard to use downstream (pixel-space video generation).
No large-scale supervision exists for object-grounded 3D motion, since 3D-captured video datasets are small and domain-limited.

Formalizes goal-conditioned 3D point motion forecasting: given a short RGB history, 3D query points on an object, and a language description of the intended action, predict each point's future metric 3D trajectory in a world frame anchored at the reference-time camera.

MolmoMotion: a VLM-based forecaster (Molmo2 backbone with per-query-point sampled visual features, anchor-relative coordinates) with two interchangeable decoding heads — autoregressive quantized-coordinate text decoding and a flow-matching DiT over continuous trajectories.

MolmoMotion-1M: 1M+ action-described, object-grounded 3D point trajectory clips auto-annotated from 1.16M unconstrained videos (grounding via MolmoPoint+SAM3, 2D tracking via AllTracker, metric 3D lifting via ViPE, object-consistency filtering/smoothing), plus PointMotionBench, a human-verified 3D forecasting benchmark.
Pretraining corpus from EgoDex, HD-EPIC, Xperience-10M, MolmoSpaces, DROID, YT-VIS, Stereo4D; 736 verbs, 5,692 objects; median clip 0.8-1.7s, ~88 retained query points/clip.
Object phrase extracted by an LLM from captions (or Molmo2-8B recaption), localized by motion-aware MolmoPoint prompting, masked by SAM3, 100 K-means query points.
Filtering uses anchor-track rigid-consistency scores, MAD outlier dropping, mean-shift auto-split, and Stereo4D-style depth-ray smoothing with multi-stride acceleration penalty.

PointMotionBench: 742 clips, 111 object categories, 61 motion types; HOT3D (mesh-pose-derived tracks) and WorldTrack (mocap tracks, custom dynamic-point clustering) with human-verified captions, plus DAVIS annotated by the pipeline with manual track verification.
Molmo2-4B (SigLIP2 ViT + Qwen3-4B) trained end-to-end; coordinates expressed relative to the first query point, quantized to millimeters for the AR head.
Flow-matching head: 36-block DiT cross-attending to per-layer LM hidden states, RoPE over point and time axes, 10 Euler steps at inference.
Stage 1: 40K steps, N=8 query points, T=8 futures at 15fps, H=3; Stage 2: 10K steps at T=32, with H=3 and H=1 variants.
AdamW, global batch 256 on 16 H100s, FSDP2, square-root dataset mixing.
Predict up to 2s at 15fps; best-of-5; metrics are 3D ADE, FDE, and PWT averaged over thresholds {0.01,0.02,0.05,0.10,0.20} m, scored only on points visible at frame 0.

Baselines: non-parametric Static and constant-velocity Extrapolate; pixel-space Wan2.2-I2V-5B and Cosmos-Predict-2.5 (generated video re-tracked into 3D); parametric 3D ObjectForesight, EgoScaler, Robot4DGen; 2D-track Track2Act lifted with GT depth.

Robotics: MolmoBot flow-matching policy (action dim 8, horizon 16) finetuned on 20K MolmoSpaces pick-and-place episodes restricted to post-grasp phases; hybrid rollout where released MolmoBot performs the grasp, then control hands off; splits SS/SU/US; matched control initialized from Molmo2-4B-Pretrain.
DROID: same 3D trajectory prediction objective finetuned on single-camera DROID videos, 12K steps, test L2 on a 10% held-out split, versus Molmo2 initialization.
Video generation: predicted 3D tracks condition DaS (CogVideoX-5B backbone), compared to unconditioned CogVideoX-5B-I2V and Wan2.2-I2V-A14B on VBench motion dimensions plus CLIP temporal consistency.
Removing per-point 2D features, replacing anchor-relative deltas with absolute world coordinates, replacing the action caption with a fixed token, and doubling query points to N=16.
Inference latency of AR vs flow-matching heads at N=8, T=32 on one A100.

key_findings.finding: Language-conditioned 3D point forecasting trained on MolmoMotion-1M substantially outperforms all prior motion-prediction paradigms on PointMotionBench, with the autoregressive head strongest.
key_findings.evidence: MolmoMotion-AR (H=3) reaches ADE 0.109 / PWT 0.444 on HOT3D, 0.143 / 0.445 on WorldTrack, and 1.227 ADE on DAVIS, versus the best competing numbers of 0.129 ADE (ObjectForesight, HOT3D only), 0.548 (Robot4DGen, WorldTrack), and 2.120 (Robot4DGen, DAVIS); Track2Act lifted 2D tracks are worst (e.g. 4.853 ADE on DAVIS).

key_findings.finding: Visually plausible pixel-space video prediction does not recover accurate metric 3D point motion, and is often worse than trivial non-parametric baselines.
key_findings.evidence: Wan2.2-5B and Cosmos-Predict re-tracked in 3D give ADE 0.200/0.225 on HOT3D and 0.852/0.831 on WorldTrack, versus 0.180 and 0.167 for simply keeping points static; the Extrapolate baseline also beats several learned methods.

key_findings.finding: The learned 3D motion prior transfers to robot manipulation, improving sample efficiency, final success, and generalization over a matched VLM initialization.
key_findings.evidence: On MolmoSpaces Franka pick-and-place with identical policy and data, MolmoMotion initialization reaches 51% success at 10K steps versus 19% for Molmo2-Pretrain and 76.3% versus 56.0% final average success, with smaller drops on unseen-object/unseen-scene splits; on DROID trajectory finetuning it starts at much lower test L2 and matches the control's 12K-step error in about 2K steps.

key_findings.finding: Anchor-relative coordinate parameterization and the language instruction are the two load-bearing design choices, not merely helpful add-ons.
key_findings.evidence: Switching to absolute world coordinates raises HOT3D ADE from 0.109 to 0.165 (PWT 0.444 to 0.276) and DAVIS ADE to 1.940; replacing the caption with a fixed token gives ADE 0.158 on HOT3D and 1.890 on DAVIS; removing the per-point 2D feature costs only 5-8% ADE, and doubling to N=16 points gains only 2-3%.

key_findings.finding: Predicted 3D trajectories serve as an effective motion-control interface for video generation, letting a small conditioned generator beat a much larger unconditioned one.
key_findings.evidence: DaS+MolmoMotion improves over its own CogVideoX-5B backbone on all five metrics and beats Wan2.2-I2V-A14B (about 2.8x parameters) on four of five, e.g. subject consistency 0.950 vs 0.940 and motion smoothness 0.990 vs 0.983, losing only on dynamic degree.
